A color change after iodine staining, from the initial yellow color to a pink color 2–3 min later, is known as the pink-color sign and is recognized as a valuable indicator for the diagnosis of ESCC 9,10 (Figure 4). This sign has been reported to dramatically improve specificity for HGIN and invasive cancer. Compared with HD-WLE, electronic and optic chromoendoscopy (i.e., NBI, BLI, FICE, and i-scan) have a higher sensitivity for the diagnosis of ESCC. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). in_text_mentions: Histopathology of the initial esophageal tumor biopsy, obtained during the EGD, revealed a keratinizing SCC (Fig. 6A) with atypical squamous cells invading the subepithelial stroma.

Histopathology of the resected LA mass showed that it predominantly consisted of necrotic fibrin and neutrophilic aggregates, suggestive of IE. Keratin plaques, which were presumed to have originated from the esophageal carcinoma, were embedded in the tissue fragments (Fig. 6B). No viable tumor cells were observed.

in_text_mentions: cal history began in 2014 after presenting with dysphagia and unintentional weight loss. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) demonstrated a 5 cm long firm friable esophageal mass at 30 cm from the incisors, Schatzki ring, and erythematous inflammation in the antrum of the stomach. Pathology revealed squamous cell carcinoma, moderately to poorly differentiated. Staging fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) showed intense hypermetabolic wall thickening of the mid esophagus with intense hypermetabolic distant metastatic lymphadenopathy consistent with stage IV disease (Figure 2).
